region: Salta and Jujuy: Quebrada de Humahuaca, Valles Calchaquíes, Cafayate
title: Argentina — Carnival of the Devils in the Painted Quebrada
subtitle: A self-drive loop from Salta through the Quebrada de Humahuaca at carnival time, the Salinas Grandes, Iruya and the Calchaquí valleys to Cafayate
summary: A 13-day Salta–Jujuy self-drive that puts the Quebrada de Humahuaca carnival (diablos, the unearthing of the pujllay doll) at the centre, with coloured hills, a high salt pan, a remote Andean village and the high-altitude wine valleys. Rainy-season road washouts are the main constraint.
introduction: Starting from Salta at 1,150 m, the car climbs by stages to the Quebrada de Humahuaca, where Purmamarca's seven-coloured hill gives way to the Tilcara fortress, Humahuaca and the striped ridge of Hornocal at 4,350 m. The trip is timed for carnival, when villages unearth a devil doll, dancers in mirrored costumes parade and offerings are made to the Pachamama. After a night in remote Iruya and a dawn on the Salinas Grandes, the loop returns over the Cuesta del Obispo to Cachi, follows RN40 through the Calchaquí valleys and ends among the vineyards of Cafayate.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is dry, empty and arranged around wadis and dunes. This route is a living Andean calendar: a village festival, indigenous Kolla salt communities, colonial adobe towns and altitude between 1,150 m and 4,350 m, with rain as the weather risk instead of heat.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Most visitors see the Quebrada on a one-day bus tour from Salta. A self-drive loop allows the carnival evenings in Tilcara and Humahuaca, a night in Iruya after the day groups leave, dawn at the Salinas Grandes and camping in Cachi and Cafayate.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: No other destination combines an intangible-heritage festival with a coloured-mountain road trip and high-altitude wine in one 13-day loop. The Atacama (D20) is a high desert across the Andes, but Salta and Jujuy are about people, festivals and valleys rather than empty salt flats and astronomy, and the second Argentina route (D29) is Patagonian ice.

duration.note: Day 1 is the overnight flight from Paris, day 13 the arrival back in Paris. Land days run from day 2 (Salta) to day 12 (departure from Salta). An Iguazú add-on would need 2 more days and exceeds the 15-day limit unless Cachi and Cafayate are dropped.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: The Quebrada carnival is this route's defining cultural experience and exists only in February. The cost is the peak of the rainy season, higher accommodation prices on carnival nights and a risk that Iruya or RN40 is cut. March is calmer, cheaper and slightly drier, but it removes the main reason to choose this region over D20 or D18. March is the lower-risk alternative: the same route without the festival.

februarySuitability.summary: Carnival (national holidays Monday 8 and Tuesday 9 February 2027) with the Quebrada's devil dances, the unearthing and offerings. Rainfall peaks (Salta about 147 mm in the month, mostly afternoon storms), roads can be cut, accommodation fills and costs more.

marchSuitability.summary: No carnival, but quieter villages, cheaper rooms and less rain (Salta about 107 mm; Humahuaca about 26 mm in the 1961–70 normals). Mud and landslide risk persists until the end of the wet season; vineyards start the harvest.

climate.regionNote: Salta city (1,150 m, airport station, 1991–2020) for the valleys; Humahuaca (3,012 m, 1961–70) for the Quebrada. Salinas Grandes (about 3,450 m) and Hornocal (4,350 m) are colder, windier and cannot be measured by these figures. Day temperatures are monthly mean highs.

february.rainfall: Salta about 147 mm (wettest month); Humahuaca about 48 mm. Storms are usually afternoon.
february.humidity: High in the Lerma valley, dry on the altiplano and in Cafayate.
february.notes: Flash floods and mud flows on the Iruya road, the Cuesta de Lipán and the Quebrada de las Conchas are the main operational risk.

march.rainfall: Salta about 107 mm; Humahuaca about 26 mm.
march.notes: Still wet season but drier; nights at Cachi and Cafayate remain mild for camping.

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: No snow expected on the route in Feb–Mar, but the Abra de Potrerillos pass on the Cuesta de Lipán (about 4,170 m, figure not verified on a fetched page) and the Iruya pass can be closed by rain, mud or fog.
climate.airQuality: Good; dust on gravel roads. Some wildfire and burning smoke risk is listed for December to March in the north by the Dutch advice.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Not a wildlife trip. Vicuña and flamingos are possible on the altiplano but are not planned.

climate.flightPriceSeasonality: Southern-summer demand keeps CDG–Buenos Aires fares higher in early February than in March. Domestic Buenos Aires–Salta fares seen for early February 2027 were about ARS 123,000 return (snapshot, not a quote).

geography.summary: The route climbs from the Lerma valley (1,150 m) into the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a coloured valley that rises to 3,000 m at Humahuaca, then to a salt pan at about 3,450 m. A second arm crosses the Cuesta del Obispo into the Calchaquí valleys and drops to Cafayate at 1,683 m.
geography.distinctive: Mineral colour on a large scale: banded Hornocal ridges up to 4,761 m, the Purmamarca hill, the red sandstone of the Quebrada de las Conchas and a white salt pan 3,450 m up, within a few hours' drive of each other.

landscapes.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca
landscapes.description: A long coloured valley with adobe villages, cardon cactus and terraces, inscribed as a World Heritage cultural landscape.

landscapes.name: Serranía de Hornocal
landscapes.description: Banded ridges rising to 4,761 m, reached by about 25 km of gravel road from Humahuaca.

landscapes.name: Salinas Grandes
landscapes.description: A salt pan of about 212 km2 at about 3,450 m, crossed by the Cuesta de Lipán road from Purmamarca.

landscapes.name: Valles Calchaquíes and Quebrada de las Conchas
landscapes.description: Cardon plateaus, adobe villages and high-altitude vineyards on RN40, then red sandstone formations along RN68.

culture.summary: Andean and Kolla culture meets colonial adobe churches. The carnival is a Pachamama festival with devil figures, music and offerings; the Pucará de Tilcara and the Salta high-altitude archaeology museum show the pre-Hispanic past.

culturalHighlights.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca carnival
culturalHighlights.description: The pujllay (a small devil doll) is unearthed at the start, diablos in mirrored costumes parade, people throw water and flour and make offerings of coca, chicha and food to the Pachamama. It closes with the burial of the doll in a secret place.

culturalHighlights.name: Pucará de Tilcara
culturalHighlights.description: A reconstructed pre-Hispanic fortified settlement above the valley, with a museum on the Quebrada's peoples. A good context stop before the carnival.

culturalHighlights.name: Museo de Arqueología de Alta Montaña, Salta
culturalHighlights.description: On the Plaza 9 de Julio. Holds Inca offerings and the mummies of three children found on a high Andean summit; confirm opening and which mummy is on display.

culturalHighlights.name: Salt-cutting communities at the Salinas Grandes
culturalHighlights.description: Kolla communities run the stops and sell salt crafts, and many oppose lithium extraction on the basin. Buying directly and asking permission before photos are the respectful approach.

culturalHighlights.name: Cachi and the Calchaquí valleys
culturalHighlights.description: Whitewashed colonial Cachi, Molinos and Angastaco: church squares, weaving, and Calchaquí heritage at the end of a mountain road.

adventureHighlights.name: Hornocal at 4,350 m
adventureHighlights.description: Gravel road from Humahuaca to a viewpoint above the striped ridges. Acclimatisation over three nights at 2,200–3,000 m first; no technical skills needed.

adventureHighlights.name: Iruya road and San Isidro walk
adventureHighlights.description: About 50 km of unpaved road to a village on a mountainside, then an 8 km walk to San Isidro. Rain can close the road for days; hence a buffer day.

adventureHighlights.name: Cuesta del Obispo and RN40 gravel
adventureHighlights.description: Switchbacks to a pass at about 3,348 m and unpaved valley roads to Cafayate. Slow driving, daylight only, with a cautious go/no-go decision after rain.

adventureHighlights.name: Camping in Cachi and Cafayate
adventureHighlights.description: Municipal or private campsites, with 2–3 nights in tents in mild valley weather.

signatureExperiences.title: The carnival of the devils in Tilcara and Humahuaca
signatureExperiences.description: Be in the Quebrada for the weekend of Saturday 6 – Tuesday 9 February: the unearthing of the pujllay doll in Tilcara, comparsas and devil dancers in the streets, offerings to the Pachamama, Humahuaca's Monday parade.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A community festival practised for the participants, not a staged show; arriving by car makes the evenings possible after day visitors have gone.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Reserve rooms for 5–9 February before the end of 2026. Check local committees' programmes in January. Do not photograph costumed dancers or offerings without a gesture of permission; water and flour are part of the play, so keep electronics in bags.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Allowance for entries to dance halls, food and tips; most street celebrations are free.

signatureExperiences.title: Serranía de Hornocal and the Quebrada's colour
signatureExperiences.description: The Purmamarca hill at dawn, the Maimará hillside and a gravel drive of about 25 km from Humahuaca to the Hornocal viewpoint above 4,000 m.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A large ridge of banded sediments visible from a road; the viewpoint is much higher than the villages, so the altitude is part of the experience.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Visit in the afternoon after nights at 2,200–3,000 m, take 3 litres of water, warm layers and a spare wheel; confirm the checkpoint fee locally (one traveller report mentions a per-vehicle fee).
signatureExperiences.costNote: Estimated checkpoint fee shared by four; unverified.

signatureExperiences.title: Dawn on the Salinas Grandes via the Cuesta de Lipán
signatureExperiences.description: Climb from Purmamarca on RN52, cross the high pass and reach the white salt pan, where community stalls sell salt crafts and families cut salt blocks.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A working landscape under debate (lithium) rather than a photo prop; the pan is at about 3,450 m.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Leave Purmamarca early, check the road (a Cuesta de Lipán mudslide at km 46 has been reported in a past rain), drive slowly at altitude and carry water. Pay community fees and buy from stalls directly.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Allowance for community fees, crafts and snacks; no official 2026 foreigner fee found.

signatureExperiences.title: Iruya, the village at the end of the gravel road
signatureExperiences.description: Drive over the pass and along the unpaved road into Iruya, sleep there and walk to San Isidro.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: A village with no road connection to the rest of Salta province, reached from Jujuy; it is tiny and slow, with carnival of its own on Monday and Tuesday.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Book two nights. Check the road with the Humahuaca tourist office the day before; if cut, spend the buffer day in Humahuaca and go to Salinas Grandes. A local hired driver is a safer alternative in heavy rain.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Allowance for the San Isidro walk guide tip and meals.

signatureExperiences.title: Cuesta del Obispo to Cafayate: the Calchaquí valleys
signatureExperiences.description: Climb the switchbacks to the Piedra del Molino pass, cross Los Cardones National Park, camp in Cachi and follow RN40 through Molinos and Angastaco to Cafayate and its torrontés vineyards.
signatureExperiences.whyDistinctive: Roads through cardon forest and adobe towns with a vineyard at the end, finishing with the red cliffs of the Quebrada de las Conchas.
signatureExperiences.howToOrganise: Daylight only; check road status each morning; camp at the municipal campsites; taste torrontés at a bodega with a designated driver or taxi.
signatureExperiences.costNote: Los Cardones fee (ARS 25,000 per person if charged) plus a winery tasting.

travelStyle.summary: A self-drive loop of about 1,450 km with two drivers, a mix of village rooms on carnival nights and camping in the valleys at the end.

transport.summary: Fly CDG to Buenos Aires (EZE), connect to Salta (SLA) through Aeroparque (AEP), then drive. The loop is mostly paved (RN9, RN52, RN68) with gravel on Hornocal, Iruya, the last stretch to Cachi and parts of RN40.

modes.description: Picked up in Salta on day 3 and returned in Salta on day 12; high clearance is advisable for Hornocal, Iruya and RN40.
Buenos Aires (AEP) to Salta (SLA), about 2 hours, by Aerolíneas Argentinas and low-cost carriers (not verified).
Local buses and minibus tours exist for the Quebrada and Salinas Grandes from Salta and Jujuy; they are the fallback if the car cannot reach a stop.

transport.carRental: Salta airport and city have Hertz and Enterprise offices; Localiza and local firms also operate (not verified). Prices found are not comparable: one aggregator gives an average pickup at about $109 a day, currency not stated. Check that the contract allows Jujuy, the gravel roads and a second driver. Cross-border into Bolivia or Chile is not planned. One-way fees are not needed.

drivingRequirements.summary: Feasible with the two licence holders. The main constraints are gravel, rain, altitude and daylight; carnival traffic and drinking add a risk on 6–9 February.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: An International Driving Permit (1949 Convention) is recommended with the French licence; rental firms may ask for it. Confirm in the rental contract.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four travellers hold car licences, so all driving is split between them. Plan for no more than about 4 hours of driving per day on gravel.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycles or scooters for anyone without the legal licence. Alternatives are local minibus tours, a hired driver for Iruya or Hornocal, and buses between towns.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Rent a high-clearance SUV or pickup with a second driver and gravel/windscreen cover, never drive at night (France Diplomatie advises against it), check road status each morning with local tourist offices, and keep a buffer day.

accommodation.summary: Salta guesthouses at the start and end, village hostales and guesthouses in the Quebrada and Iruya, and three nights in tents at municipal or private campsites.

camping.summary: Campsites exist in Purmamarca, Cachi and Cafayate (user reports; prices from unknown dates). Nights at altitude are cold and carnival campsites are loud. Camping is planned in the valleys on days 7, 9 and 10. Rain can flood sites; have a room fallback.

physicalDifficulty.label: moderate
physicalDifficulty.summary: Mostly driving and short walks. The challenge is altitude: nights at 2,200–3,000 m and day visits at 3,450–4,350 m. Headaches are likely for some travellers, so plan slow ascent, hydration and no alcohol on the first day above 3,000 m.

itinerary.summary: Fly to Salta, drive north into the Quebrada for carnival, detour to Hornocal and Iruya, cross the Salinas Grandes, then return to Salta and loop through Cachi and Cafayate before flying home.

assumptions: Four travellers share two rooms and one rental car; two of them drive. The car is rented for 9 days, picked up on day 3 and returned on day 12.

Peso figures use about ARS 1,700 per euro, the D29 basis (official dollar about ARS 1,465 in August 2026 and the euro about US$1.15–1.17). A current euro quote was not found, and peso prices rise faster than the currency falls, so peso-based lines may be understated by February 2027.

Carnival-night rooms (days 3 to 6) are assumed to cost about 65% more than standard rooms; this is an assumption, not an observed price. Camping is assumed on days 7, 9 and 10, and rooms on all other nights.

The Iguazú Falls add-on is not in the budget: the Argentine park ticket for foreigners is reported at ARS 60,000 (about €35) from June 2026, plus a return Salta–Puerto Iguazú flight by Buenos Aires (estimate €150–250 per person), two nights and transfers; roughly €300–450 per person and 2 extra days.
Contingency is applied to local costs only (not flights). Prices are November 2026 estimates, not quotes.

budget.exceptionalJustification: The realistic total is above €2,000 mostly because of the €1,050 flight to Buenos Aires plus a domestic leg and a rental car for four. The justification is the carnival: a community festival that takes place only in February, combined with Hornocal, the Salinas Grandes, Iruya and Cafayate in one loop. Camping and a short 13-day plan keep the local cost per person near €1,380.

scenarioNotes.economical: Compact SUV, hostales at minimum carnival rates, camping on three nights, supermarket lunches, no guides. Carnival rooms may not be available at this rate.
scenarioNotes.realistic: Mid-size SUV with tyre cover, four carnival nights in hostales, three standard nights in Salta, three camping nights, restaurant meals, a winery tasting. This is the headline.
scenarioNotes.comfortable: 4x4 pickup, a hired driver for Iruya, rooms every night, estancia or bodega stays at carnival rates and a guided day.

security.summary: No advisory found for Salta or Jujuy against travel; the reviewed pages name only ordinary risks (road safety, crime in big cities, protests and blockades, earthquakes, rainy-season floods and landslides, altitude). Terrorism, armed conflict and kidnapping are not identified as material on this route.
security.assessedRoute: Salta city, RN9 to Jujuy, Purmamarca, Tilcara, Humahuaca, Hornocal, Iruya, RN52 to the Salinas Grandes, RP33 (Cuesta del Obispo, Los Cardones, Cachi), RN40 to Cafayate and RN68 back to Salta. The Bolivian border at La Quiaca and Villazón is not on the route; Iruya lies in the mountains not far from the border (distance not verified).

regionalRestrictions: No restrictions found for Salta, Jujuy, Cachi or Cafayate on the pages read.
Rental cars generally cannot cross borders; the Bolivian border is not planned.
Road blockades by protests or strikes can occur; the Dutch advice says travel within the country is often impossible on strike days.
ordinaryRisks: Road safety: poor driving standards and no night driving (France Diplomatie); gravel, cattle and fog on mountain roads

Rainy-season hazards: mudslides and flash floods on the Iruya road, the Cuesta de Lipán (a km-46 slide has been reported), RP33 and RN68; Iruya has had a mud flow that stranded tourists in a previous year
Altitude sickness at 3,000–4,350 m; pulmonary or cerebral oedema is possible above 3,000 m
Carnival: water, flour and foam throwing, crowds and drunk drivers on 6–9 February
Theft from parked rental cars and in cities; hantavirus and dengue are present in Argentina
Fuel and cash: few fuel stations and ATMs beyond Humahuaca, Cachi and Cafayate (not verified)
security.medicalAccess: Hospitals in Salta and Jujuy; small health posts in villages. Iruya, Humahuaca, Cachi and Cafayate have basic care; serious cases go to Salta or Jujuy, or are evacuated. Emergency numbers: 107 ambulance, 911 police.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Insurance must cover altitude to 4,500 m, medical evacuation and rental-car excess; check exclusions for unpaved roads and for injuries linked to alcohol during carnival.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all advisories before booking and two weeks before departure. Triggers: any change to the France or FCDO country pages, El Niño flood and storm alerts, road closures on RN9, RN52, RP33, RN40 or the Iruya road, blockades or strikes, and a change in fuel supply. The US State Department page returned HTTP 403 on 28 Nov 2026 and was not read; Smartraveller was read via a search snippet.

practicalRequirements.visa: French citizens do not need a visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days according to the Argentine rules summarised in D29; confirm for each passport on the Argentine government site.
practicalRequirements.entry: Check the arrival formalities for your nationality; Smartraveller mentions enhanced border security measures with some travellers delayed or refused entry.
practicalRequirements.passportValidity: The Dutch advice states a passport valid for at least 6 months; confirm for your nationality.
permits: Los Cardones National Park fee (ARS 25,000 for general visitors, collection date unclear)
Local fees at Salinas Grandes, Hornocal and the Pucará (amounts not found)
practicalRequirements.insurance: Medical, evacuation and altitude cover, rental excess cover and a second-driver clause.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile coverage is expected in towns and weak on gravel roads, the Salinas Grandes and Iruya; buy a local SIM or eSIM and download maps (not verified).
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards are common in Salta and Cafayate, but small villages and campsites need pesos in cash. Check the current exchange-rate regime before travel.
practicalRequirements.medical: No mandatory vaccines; check routine vaccines and measles status (France Diplomatie alert), and dengue and hantavirus advice. Discuss acetazolamide and altitude with a doctor.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fill up in Salta, Jujuy, Humahuaca, Cachi and Cafayate; availability in Iruya and Molinos is not verified.
equipment: Layers, rain jacket and warm hat for 4,350 m and cold nights
Sun protection (strong UV at altitude), sunglasses, refillable bottles
Tents, sleeping bags rated to about 5 °C and mats for three nights
Offline maps, torch, spare wheel check and a small tool kit
IDP and driving licences for the two drivers; cash in pesos

advantages: Carnival is a living, community festival that cannot be seen in the other portfolio routes in February
Gradual acclimatisation: Salta 1,150 m, Purmamarca 2,200 m, Tilcara 2,460 m, Humahuaca 3,000 m
Strong geographic variety in short distances: coloured hills, a salt pan, red gorges and vineyards
No visa for French citizens (to confirm) and no conflict-related advisory
Camping in mild valley nights and a Salta hub for the car
disadvantages: Peak of the rainy season: landslides and flash floods can close the Iruya road, RN52 and RN40
Carnival nights are expensive and sell out; rooms must be booked in 2026
The flight to Buenos Aires plus a domestic leg dominates the budget (about €1,050 plus about €105)
Altitude headaches are likely on days 5, 6 and 8, and gravel driving limits distances
The festival programme for 2027 is unconfirmed; dates in this file are inferred from 2026
